content:
The [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Returns on a systematic investment plan in mutual funds. Enter your monthly investment, expected annual return and duration and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) invests a fixed amount in a mutual fund every month. A SIP calculator estimates what those regular investments may grow to. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the SIP Calculator

Start by entering your monthly investment, then entering your expected annual return (%) and finally entering your duration (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your monthly investment.
2. Enter your expected annual return (%).
3. Enter your duration (years).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

FV = P × ((1 + i)ⁿ − 1) ÷ i × (1 + i), where i is the monthly return and n the number of instalments.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Investing 5,000 a month for 10 years at 12% may grow to about 11.6 lakh on an investment of 6 lakh. Try the same figures in the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Monthly investment: 5000, Expected annual return: 12 %, Duration: 10 years), the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) returns Maturity value: 1,161,695.38, Amount invested: 600,000, Estimated returns: 561,695.38. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Stay invested through market dips — that's when SIPs buy more units.
- Use a step-up SIP to raise contributions yearly.
- Returns are not guaranteed; equity funds fluctuate.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is SIP return guaranteed?

No. Mutual fund returns depend on markets; the calculator assumes a constant rate for illustration. Try it with your own numbers in the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is a good SIP duration?

For equity funds, 7 years or longer smooths out market volatility. Try it with your own numbers in the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the SIP Calculator use?

FV = P × ((1 + i)ⁿ − 1) ÷ i × (1 + i), where i is the monthly return and n the number of instalments. You can see it in action in the [SIP Calculator](/sip-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the SIP Calculator?

Just Monthly investment, Expected annual return and Duration. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
